findings.title: load('sotus') serves the nips_model pickle (stale sklearn text model), not the documented SOTU speeches -- duplicate Drive id in EXAMPLE_DATA
findings.description: hypertools/io/load.py documents "`sotus` is a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018", but EXAMPLE_DATA['sotus'] and EXAMPLE_DATA['nips_model'] contain the IDENTICAL Google Drive id ('1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm', load.py lines 24 and 27), so load('sotus') downloads/unpickles a CountVectorizer->LatentDirichletAllocation sklearn Pipeline (verified: cached ~/hypertools_data/sotus and ~/hypertools_data/nips_model are byte-identical, MD5 6a350ab8d85db34e7b924ac8a7f2a19b). Because 'sotus' does not end with '_model', load() does not take the model branch, but the Pipeline has no get_data(), so the model object is returned as if it were data. Even printing it crashes (see -002). examples/plot_sotus.py already contains the comment "Note: 'sotus' loads a text processing model, not the actual SOTU speeches" -- the workaround is known, but the load() docstring still promises speeches, so any scientist following the documented API gets a broken/wrong object. Also 'nips', 'nips_model', and 'sotus_model' are absent from the docstring's dataset list.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; s = hyp.load('sotus'); print(type(s)); print(s)"
findings.expected: A collection of State of the Union speeches (text data) per the load() docstring
findings.actual: type -> <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'> (len 2: CountVectorizer -> LatentDirichletAllocation); print(s) -> AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'; MD5(~/hypertools_data/sotus) == MD5(~/hypertools_data/nips_model) == 6a350ab8d85db34e7b924ac8a7f2a19b

findings.title: Hosted *_model pickles are sklearn 1.0.2 artifacts: under the pinned sklearn 1.8, loading warns InconsistentVersionWarning and repr() of the returned model raises AttributeError
findings.description: load('wiki_model')/load('sotus_model')/load('nips_model') unpickle sklearn Pipelines created with scikit-learn 1.0.2. Under the repo venv's scikit-learn 1.8.0 each load emits sklearn's InconsistentVersionWarning ('Trying to unpickle estimator ... from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0'), and simply printing/repr-ing the returned object -- the first thing a user does with it -- raises AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'. wiki_model.transform(['text']) still works ((1, 50) topic vector, so the docstring claim about transforming text holds), but the objects are only partially functional and every display path crashes. The hosted pickles need re-saving under a modern sklearn (or load() needs a compatibility shim/documented caveat).
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; m = hyp.load('sotus_model'); print(m)"
findings.expected: A usable, printable fitted text-processing model (docstring: 'It can be used to transform text to topic vectors.')
findings.actual: InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator CountVectorizer from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0 ... then RAISED AttributeError: 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'

findings.title: hyp.align on a single (non-list) dataset returns a 1-element list, contradicting its documented single-item return and the reduce/normalize convention
findings.description: hypertools/align/align.py's Returns section: 'aligned : list of numpy arrays (or a single array) -- The aligned data, in the same list/single-item shape as `data` (matching hyp.reduce/hyp.cluster/hyp.manip...)'. Actual: hyp.align(single_2d_array) and hyp.align(single_DataFrame) both return a LIST containing one array. hyp.reduce/hyp.normalize return a bare array for single input, so the documented cross-module consistency claim is false and code like hyp.align(x).shape fails with AttributeError.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; r = hyp.align(np.random.randn(50, 5)); print(type(r), len(r), type(r[0]))"
findings.expected: A single numpy array (same single-item shape as the input), per the docstring
findings.actual: <class 'list'> 1 <class 'numpy.ndarray'> -- align(single) exact type -> ('list', ['ndarray'])

findings.title: analyze()/load() normalize param text says "z-scored across lists (default)" but their actual default is None (no normalization)
findings.description: hypertools/tools/analyze.py and hypertools/io/load.py both document normalize as: "If set to 'across', the columns of the input data will be z-scored across lists (default)." In both signatures the default is None, which SKIPS normalization entirely ('across' is only the default of hypertools.tools.normalize.normalize itself). A user reading analyze()'s docstring would believe data is z-scored by default; it is not (verified: hyp.analyze(x, reduce='PCA', ndims=2) does not z-score input).

findings.actual: (data, manip=None, normalize=None, reduce=None, ...) vs doc line "If set to 'across', the columns of the input data will be z-scored across lists (default)."

findings.title: analyze() docstring claims cluster() 'returns per-dataset labels alongside the transformed data in one call' -- cluster() actually returns one flat label list and no transformed data
findings.description: hypertools/tools/analyze.py cluster param: 'to get labels split PER dataset, call hypertools.cluster.cluster.cluster directly (it returns per-dataset labels alongside the transformed data in one call).' Verified actual behavior of hyp.cluster([A(60 rows), B(50 rows)], n_clusters=3): returns a single flat list of 110 labels over the row-concatenated data (not split per dataset), and returns only labels (data is returned only with return_model=True, and even then the second element is the model, not transformed data). findings.title: Signature/docstring parameter drift: analyze(random_state), cluster(random_state), normalize(internal), manip's five cross-module kwargs, df2mat(return_labels) all undocumented; load() documents params out of signature order
findings.description: Enumerated every documented parameter against every public signature outside plot/. Drift found: (1) analyze() signature has random_state=None -- absent from its Parameters section (works: tested with TSNE); (2) cluster() signature has random_state=None -- absent from Parameters (works: injected into KMeans/GaussianMixture); (3) normalize() signature has internal=False -- absent from Parameters (reduce/analyze document theirs); (4) manip() signature has normalize/reduce/ndims/align/cluster cross-module kwargs -- none are in its Parameters section though they work (tested manip(A, model='Smooth', reduce='PCA', ndims=2) -> (80, 2)) and every sibling dispatcher documents them; (5) df2mat() return_labels is only mentioned inside Returns, not in Parameters; (6) load() documents normalize before reduce/ndims/align, mismatching signature order (dataset, reduce, ndims, align, normalize, ...). Everything else matched.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import inspect; import hypertools as hyp; from hypertools.tools.analyze import analyze; from hypertools.cluster.cluster import cluster; from hypertools.tools.normalize import normalize; from hypertools.manip.manip import manip; print(inspect.signature(analyze)); print('random_state' in analyze.__doc__); print(inspect.signature(cluster)); print('random_state' in cluster.__doc__); print('internal' in normalize.__doc__.split('Returns')[0].split('Parameters')[1]); print(inspect.signature(manip)); print('align :' in manip.__doc__)"
findings.expected: Every signature parameter documented in its Parameters section
findings.actual: analyze: random_state in signature, 'random_state' not in docstring -> False; cluster: same -> False; normalize Parameters section lacks internal; manip docstring Parameters = data/model/return_model/**kwargs only

findings.title: normalize() invalid-mode error is an AssertionError naming a nonexistent parameter 'scale_type'
findings.description: hyp.normalize(x, normalize='bogus') fails via a bare assert: "AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer." Problems: (a) AssertionError instead of ValueError (and silently DISABLED under python -O, letting invalid modes fall through to 'if normalize in [False, None]' and then Normalizer's late ValueError); (b) 'scale_type' is not the parameter's name (it is 'normalize'); (c) 'none' is presented as a string-ish option. Every sibling dispatcher raises ValueError naming the real kwarg.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.normalize(np.random.randn(10, 3), normalize='bogus')"
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize must be 'across', 'within', 'row', False, None, or a fitted Normalizer; got 'bogus'
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: assert-based validation raises AssertionError where docstrings promise ValueError (manip transformers, Manipulator.fit, Forecaster.fit) and is stripped under python -O
findings.description: smooth.transformer / zscore.transformer / (manip) normalize.transformer docstrings each document "Raises: ValueError -- If `axis` is missing from kwargs..." but the code is `assert 'axis' in kwargs.keys(), ValueError('Must specify axis')`, which raises AssertionError (verified) and vanishes under `python -O`. The same `assert cond, ValueError(...)` anti-pattern (the ValueError instance is just the assert MESSAGE, never raised) appears in manip/common.py Manipulator.fit ('cannot manipulate an empty dataset', 'fit function must return a dictionary'), predict/common.py Forecaster.fit and _infer_step, manip/normalize.py fitter (min<max), manip/resample.py fitter/transformer, and manip/smooth.py transformer's kernel_width>0 check. predict.common.resolve_t was already converted to real raises (its comment cites this exact hazard) -- the rest were not.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, pandas as pd; from hypertools.manip.smooth import transformer; transformer(pd.DataFrame(np.random.randn(20, 3)))"
findings.expected: ValueError (as documented in the transformer docstrings), robust under -O
findings.actual: AssertionError: Must specify axis

findings.title: Error messages steer users toward the DEPRECATED {'model','params'} dict form
findings.description: The library deprecates {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} everywhere (DeprecationWarning on use, verified), yet: (a) reduce()'s malformed-dict error says "pass the model as the value of the 'model' key and a dictionary of custom params as the value of the 'params' key" (verified with reduce={}); (b) manip/impute/predict unknown-model errors advertise "or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}" as the suggested dict shape. Following the library's own error guidance immediately triggers a DeprecationWarning. Suggest naming the canonical {'model','args','kwargs'} triple instead.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.reduce(np.random.randn(20, 5), reduce={}, ndims=2)"
findings.expected: Errors recommending the canonical {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} spec
findings.actual: ValueError: If passing a dictionary, pass the model as the value of the "model" key and a                 dictionary of custom params as the value of the "params" key. ; manip: "(or pass a dict {'model': ..., 'params': {...}}, a Manipulator subclass, ...)"

findings.title: No runnable Examples on any primary public function outside plot/ except load()/Pipeline/lsl_stream
findings.description: Grep for '>>>' across hypertools/ (excluding plot/, _externals/, external/): only 3 files contain examples -- io/load.py, core/pipeline.py (marked +SKIP), io/lsl.py (marked +SKIP). The primary public API functions reduce(), align() (both APIs), analyze(), normalize(), cluster(), manip(), predict(), impute(), describe(), apply_model(), save(), format_data(), df2mat(), missing_inds() have NO Examples section at all. Against the stated 1.0 release bar ('every public function documented with a runnable example'), this is a systematic gap. All of these functions were verified to work in this audit, so examples are cheap to add from the tested snippets.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && grep -rln '>>>' hypertools/ --include='*.py' | grep -v plot | grep -v _externals | grep -v external/
findings.expected: Runnable Examples on every primary public function
findings.actual:
hypertools/core/pipeline.py
hypertools/io/load.py
hypertools/io/lsl.py  (3 files total)

findings.title: save() silently swallows **kwargs (protocol=, compression=, typos) and has a one-line docstring with no Parameters/Returns
findings.description: hypertools/io/save.py: def save(obj, fname, **kwargs) -- kwargs are accepted and completely ignored. hyp.save(A, f, protocol=5, compression='gzip', bogus=1) runs without error and without effect, so a user believing they set a pickle protocol or compression gets neither, and typos are never caught. The docstring is the single line 'Pickle `obj` to `fname`.' -- no Parameters/Returns/Examples, no mention that kwargs are ignored (the module docstring's export note doesn't reach help(hyp.save)). Suggest either forwarding protocol= to pickle.dump or rejecting unknown kwargs.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.save(np.eye(3), '/tmp/x.pkl', protocol=5, compression='gzip', bogus=1); print('accepted silently')"
findings.expected: TypeError on unknown kwargs (or honored protocol=), and a real docstring
findings.actual: accepted silently -- kwargs ignored; save.__doc__ == 'Pickle `obj` to `fname`.'

findings.title: load() of a corrupt local pickle leaks raw 'ValueError: unsupported pickle protocol' -- the friendly HypertoolsIOError/legacy hint only catches pickle.UnpicklingError
findings.description: hypertools/io/load.py _load_local wraps pickle.loads in `except pickle.UnpicklingError` to raise the friendly HypertoolsIOError ('If ... was created with hypertools<0.8.0, pass legacy=True'). But pickle.loads raises ValueError (e.g. 'unsupported pickle protocol: 104') or EOFError/AttributeError for many corruption modes, which escape uncaught, so the documented guidance never appears for a truncated/corrupt .pkl/.geo file.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp, pathlib; p = pathlib.Path('/tmp/corrupt_audit.pkl'); p.write_bytes(b'\x80hello-not-valid'); hyp.load(str(p))"
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError: Failed to load DataGeometry object from ... pass legacy=True ...
findings.actual: ValueError: unsupported pickle protocol: 104

findings.title: describe(): garbled summary line, unconditional 'large data' warning on any input size, and show=True displays via plt.show() without returning the figure
findings.description: hypertools/reduce/describe.py: (a) summary line reads 'Create plot describing covariance with as a function of number of dimensions' -- 'covariance with as a function' is garbled (and the metric is correlation of pairwise distances, not covariance); (b) warnings.warn('When input data is large, this computation can take a long time.') fires unconditionally -- verified on a 20x4 input; (c) with show=True the matplotlib branch ends in plt.show() and the dict is the only return, so under Agg users get 'FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown' and there is no handle to save the figure (hyp.plot returns a Figure; describe cannot). Also get_corr(reduced, alldims)'s parameters are passed swapped at its call site (harmless -- Pearson r is symmetric -- but misleading).
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.describe(np.random.randn(20, 4), show=False)"
findings.expected: Accurate summary; a size-gated (or removed) warning; a way to obtain the figure
findings.actual: UserWarning: When input data is large, this computation can take a long time. (on 20x4 data); with show=True under Agg: UserWarning: FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive, and thus cannot be shown

findings.title: Smooth docstring says non-integer kernel_width is 'rounded up'; actual behavior rounds to NEAREST integer (then bumps evens by 1)
findings.description: hypertools/manip/smooth.py Smooth docstring: 'kernel_width : int ... non-integer/even values are rounded up with a warning.' Actual (transformer): non-integers are rounded to the NEAREST integer (warning text: 'Rounding smoothing kernel width to the nearest integer'), then even results get +1. So 11.4 -> 11 (rounded DOWN), 10.4 -> 10 -> 11. Verified with kernel_width=10.4 producing both warnings.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -W always -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; hyp.manip(np.random.randn(80, 4), model='Smooth', kernel_width=10.4)"
findings.expected: Docstring matching the round-to-nearest-then-odd behavior
findings.actual: UserWarning: Rounding smoothing kernel width to the nearest integer + UserWarning: Increasing smoothing kernel width by 1 (must be odd)

findings.title: missing_inds() Returns omits the None sentinel (clean single array returns None, clean list entries are None)
findings.description: hypertools/tools/missing_inds.py Returns: 'inds : list, or list of lists -- A list of indices representing rows with missing data. If a list of numpy arrays is passed, a list of lists will be returned.' Actual: an array WITHOUT missing data yields None -- a clean single array returns bare None (not a list), and in the list case clean datasets appear as None entries (e.g. [array([2]), None]). Code iterating 'for i in missing_inds(x)' on a clean array crashes on None. Return type is also numpy arrays, not lists.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np; from hypertools.tools.missing_inds import missing_inds; A = np.random.randn(60, 6); B = A.copy(); B[2, 3] = np.nan; print(missing_inds(A)); print(missing_inds([B, A]))"
findings.expected: Documented None sentinel / ndarray return types
findings.actual: None ; [array([2]), None]

findings.title: procrustes() leaks numpy PendingDeprecationWarning (np.matrix) on every call
findings.description: hypertools.align.procrustes.procrustes(source, target) works (verified: maps spiral[0] exactly onto spiral[1], residual 0.0) but emits 'PendingDeprecationWarning: the matrix subclass is not the recommended way to represent matrices or deal with linear algebra' from its np.matrix usage on every call. np.matrix is slated for removal; user-facing noise today, breakage risk later.
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -W always -c "import hypertools as hyp; from hypertools.align.procrustes import procrustes; s = hyp.load('spiral'); procrustes(s[0], s[1])"
findings.expected: No deprecation noise; ndarray-based implementation
findings.actual: PendingDeprecationWarning: the matrix subclass is not the recommended way to represent matrices or deal with linear algebra (see https://... )

findings.title: apply_model('KMeans') in default mode='auto' returns cluster-distance space, not labels -- documented but surprising next to hyp.cluster
findings.description: apply_model's mode='auto' preference order (predict_proba -> fit_transform -> fit_predict) means KMeans (which HAS fit_transform) returns the (n_samples, n_clusters) cluster-DISTANCE matrix -- verified: hyp.apply_model(A_60x8, 'KMeans') -> (60, 8) distances (sklearn default 8 clusters), while hyp.cluster(A) returns 60 labels. The behavior matches apply_model's own docstring, but a scientist reaching for 'apply KMeans' almost always wants labels; nothing in the docstring warns that clusterers with fit_transform never reach the fit_predict branch. Suggest a docstring note (or preferring fit_predict for clusterer-registry names).
findings.repro: cd /Users/jmanning/hypertools && env MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp; A = np.random.randn(60, 8); print(np.asarray(hyp.apply_model(A, 'KMeans')).shape); print(len(hyp.cluster(A)))"
findings.expected: Labels, or an explicit docstring warning for clusterers under mode='auto'
findings.actual: (60, 8) cluster-distance matrix from apply_model vs 60 labels from hyp.cluster
